STRATEGIC REPORT
FOR THE YEAR ENDED 31 MARCH 2025
- 1 -
The directors present the strategic report for the year ended 31 March 2025.
Review of the business
The group operates a network of community pharmacies across England and Wales, providing NHS and private pharmaceutical services, clinical consultations, and healthcare advice. The 2024/25 financial year represented a pivotal period for the community pharmacy sector, characterised by the successful launch and rapid expansion of the Pharmacy First scheme in January 2024, alongside significant ongoing financial pressures that have affected the entire sector.
The group has continued its expansion during the period, growing its base of pharmacy branches, delivering numbers of NHS service consultations and dispensing a growing volume of prescriptions, reflecting our commitment to accessible, high-quality care. The Pharmacy First scheme has been particularly successful, with participating pharmacies nationally delivering over 1.9 million consultations for seven common conditions by the end of the financial year. Our branches have embraced this expanded clinical role, alongside increased delivery of the Pharmacy Contraception Service and Hypertension Case Finding Service consultations.
The operating environment has remained extremely challenging throughout 2024/25 but the group maintained its service levels and continued to invest in digital transformation, workforce development, and patient safety. Despite sector-wide challenges, the group's financial performance during 2024/25 was supported by the 4.1% uplift in NHS funding under the Community Pharmacy Contractual Framework (CPCF), rising to 7.5% when Pharmacy First funding was included. However, despite this increase, the pressures of sustained inflation, increased National Insurance contributions, national living wage increases and a shortages of key skills have had an impact on margins across the sector.
Non-financial Key Performance Indicators
Non-financial key performance indicators (KPIs) for the year included:
Number of NHS and private prescriptions dispensed
Volume of clinical consultations delivered, including:
Pharmacy First clinical pathway consultations (seven common conditions)
Contraception service consultations (both initiation and continuation)
Hypertension case finding consultations
Blood pressure check service consultations
Patient satisfaction and service accessibility metrics
Staff retention and training completion rates, including clinical examination skills training
Digital service uptake and efficiency improvements
Medicine supply management

STRATEGIC REPORT (CONTINUED)
FOR THE YEAR ENDED 31 MARCH 2025
- 2 -
Strategic Focus
The group's focus remains centred on providing essential medicines, clinical services, and public health interventions within local communities. Our strategy for the period ahead is to:
Maximise opportunities from the Pharmacy First scheme and other clinical services, following the April 2025 fee increases (Pharmacy First consultations rising from £15 to £17, and Pharmacy Contraception Service fees increasing from £18 to £25)
Continue to expand clinical service provision in line with NHS priorities and the government's shift from hospital to community care
Invest in digital infrastructure to streamline operations, improve patient experience, and integrate with NHS systems for enhanced information sharing
Strengthen workforce skills and capacity through ongoing training, recruitment, and retention initiatives, recognising the national shortage of pharmacists
Enhance operational efficiency and cost control to address the significant funding gap and mitigate ongoing inflationary pressures
Collaborate with NHS and local partners to support integrated care and public health outcomes, positioning community pharmacy as a cornerstone of the government's 10 Year Health Plan
Advocate actively for sustainable long-term funding that reflects the true Full Economic Cost of service delivery
SHARIEF GROUP LIMITED
STRATEGIC REPORT (CONTINUED)
FOR THE YEAR ENDED 31 MARCH 2025
- 3 -
Principal risks and uncertainties
The group faces several principal risks and uncertainties which are consistent with other businesses operating in the community pharmacy sector. The financial year 2024/25 has highlighted the severity of these risks, particularly regarding sector viability and sustainability:
Risk Area
Description
Mitigation Strategies
Funding Gap & Financial Viability
Despite the welcome funding increases for 2025/26 (CPCF rising to £3.073 billion, representing a 19.7% like-for-like increase on 2023/24 levels, plus £215 million for Pharmacy First and related services), independent economic analysis confirms a significant gap remains between funding and the Full Economic Cost of service delivery. The sector has experienced approximately 30% reduction in funding in real terms since 2015.
Rigorous cost control and operational efficiency measures, service prioritisation, active engagement with Government and NHS England on the commitment to work towards a sustainable funding model, strategic review of branch network to focus on viable locations, and close monitoring of the announced £30 million Pharmacy Quality Scheme from April 2025.
Workforce Challenges
National shortages of pharmacists and support staff, alongside rising wage pressures. Locum pharmacist costs have increased dramatically, and staffing costs overall have grown significantly. The sector faces difficulty recruiting and retaining qualified professionals. Increased National Insurance contributions and national living wage increases add further cost pressures.
Investment in recruitment, competitive remuneration packages, staff development and training (including clinical examination skills for Pharmacy First delivery), retention initiatives, and workforce planning to manage service delivery within available resources.
Regulatory & Policy Change
Ongoing changes to NHS pharmacy contract requirements and service specifications, including Pharmacy First implementation, updates to Hypertension Case Finding Service aligned with NICE guidelines, and evolving requirements for digital integration and information sharing. The government's 10 Year Health Plan will place increasing expectations on community pharmacy's role in primary care.
Robust compliance processes, regular policy monitoring, proactive engagement with NHS staff and ongoing staff training on new service requirements, and stakeholder engagement to influence policy development.
Operational Pressures
Continued supply chain disruptions and medicine shortages, with 94% of pharmacies nationally reporting increased time spent sourcing medicines. IT system integration challenges, particularly regarding Pharmacy First digital infrastructure and GP record access. Delivery of services within monthly consultation caps and activity thresholds.
Diversification of suppliers, robust supplier relationships, digital system upgrades, business continuity planning, effective medicine sourcing strategies, and proactive management of service delivery against contractual requirements.

STRATEGIC REPORT (CONTINUED)
FOR THE YEAR ENDED 31 MARCH 2025
- 4 -
Digital & Cybersecurity
Increasing reliance on digital systems for Pharmacy First delivery, electronic referrals from NHS 111 and GP practices, integration with GP records, and associated cyber risks.
Enhanced cybersecurity measures, staff training on information governance, investment in IT resilience, and compliance with NHS digital standards and information sharing protocols.
Increased Demand & Service Pressure
Growing prescription volumes (forecast to exceed 1.2 billion in 2025/26), increased clinical service consultations, and patient expectations for accessible services, alongside resource constraints and longer dispensing times affecting patient experience.
Efficiency improvements through digital solutions, effective staff deployment, service planning to manage demand within capacity, and clear communication with patients about service availability.
The group remains committed to navigating these significant risks through resilience, digital innovation, operational excellence, and strategic agility.
Key performance indicators
In addition to its suite of non-financial KPIs, the Directors assess the financial performance of the business by monitoring revenue growth, gross margin, EBITDA generation, and cashflow. These KPIs are monitored monthly to ensure that the group maintains its forward momentum and continues to generate sustainable EBITDA and cashflow despite the challenging sector-wide profitability environment.

The business has continued its growth trajectory during the financial year, and while wider sector challenges have impacted margins in the immediate term, operational improvement is evidenced in the 2024/25 performance. Continued performance improvement despite sector-wide pressures reflect effective operational management and the benefits of scale.
Future and subsequent events
The group continues to pursue growth opportunities through acquisition and through strong relationships with its suppliers to generate a more efficient supply chain. This approach allows the group to mitigate risks throughout its portfolio and develop efficiencies through its core services to obtain strategic advantage. The group's scale provides resilience in navigating the challenging funding environment that has affected smaller operators across the sector.
The group maintains focus on operational excellence, cost discipline, and maximising income opportunities from the expanded range of clinical services, particularly Pharmacy First and related advanced services, to sustain financial viability in the context of the confirmed funding gap.
Future Outlook & Subsequent Events
The Board of Directors and Management continue to pursue a strategy of selective growth through both the development of existing branches and the acquisition of branches with opportunities for synergy within the portfolio, while maintaining disciplined financial management.
During the 2024/25 financial year, the business continued to generate additional value from its established and well-respected brand together with its existing operating infrastructure. The group's expanded scale provides enhanced resilience against the sector's financial pressures.

- 5 -
2025/26 Funding Settlement
In April 2025, a significant funding settlement for community pharmacy was announced for 2025/26, representing the largest uplift across the entire NHS:
CPCF baseline funding rising to £3.073 billion (19.7% increase on 2023/24 on a like-for-like basis)
£215 million confirmed for Pharmacy First and other Primary Care Access Recovery Plan services
£193 million write-off of historic medicines margin over-delivery
Single Activity Fee (SAF) increased from £1.27 to £1.46
Pharmacy First consultation fee increased from £15 to £17
Pharmacy Contraception Service fees increased from £18 to £25
Reinstatement of a targeted Pharmacy Quality Scheme worth £30 million
This settlement represents a welcome first step towards sector stability and the first significant investment in core funding for over 10 years.
Strategic Priorities for 2025/26
The group will focus on:
Maximising income opportunities from the Pharmacy First scheme and expanded clinical services, following the fee increases and the reinstatement of the Pharmacy Quality Scheme
Leveraging digital investments to improve efficiency, integrate with NHS systems, and enhance patient care
Managing ongoing cost pressures through operational excellence, efficient medicine sourcing, and prudent financial management
Continuing workforce development to support expanded clinical service delivery
Actively engaging with sector representatives, Government, and NHS England to advocate for sustainable long-term funding that reflects the Full Economic Cost of service delivery
Monitoring and responding to the development of the government's 10 Year Health Plan and its implications for community pharmacy's expanded role in primary care
Promoting the Success of the Company
This statement by the Board of Directors describes how they have approached their responsibilities under s172(1)(a) to (f) of the Companies Act 2006 during the financial period ending 31 March 2025.
The stakeholders of the group include employees, patients and service users, commissioners and the NHS, suppliers, and the wider communities we serve.
The directors consider they have acted in good faith to promote the success of the company on behalf of its stakeholders, in relation to the matters set out in s172 of the Act, particularly during a period of unprecedented challenge for the community pharmacy sector.
The directors monitor and review strategic objectives against long-term plans. Regular reviews are held across key business areas, including financial performance, risks and opportunities, health & safety, human resources, and operations. The company's performance and progress are reviewed regularly at department, senior leadership, and Board meetings, with particular attention paid to the evolving regulatory and funding landscape affecting the sector.
The fundamental principle in the governance of the company is ensuring transparent conduct which reflects fairness in all dealings with employees, patients, commissioners, and suppliers.
SHARIEF GROUP LIMITED
STRATEGIC REPORT (CONTINUED)
FOR THE YEAR ENDED 31 MARCH 2025
- 6 -
Employees
The Directors develop and enact policies to promote diversity, equity, and inclusion amongst employees. The group observes both formal and informal processes to actively engage its employees. These include employee performance reviews and appraisals, regular communications through email and team meetings, and regular branch visits by senior management. The Directors use these opportunities, together with other informal meetings, to gauge the views and needs of employees, which are reflected, wherever possible, in the decision-making process.
The group recognises the exceptional dedication of pharmacy teams during a period of intense pressure on the sector. Investment in staff training, particularly in clinical examination skills to support Pharmacy First delivery, demonstrates our commitment to workforce development. The group remains focused on recruitment and retention strategies to address the national pharmacist shortage and ensure sustainable service delivery.
Patients, Customers and Service Users
Delivering high-quality patient care and customer service is a key pillar of the values of the business. The Directors strongly believe in treating patients and customers fairly and with respect, always ensuring that products and services meet their needs and are delivered safely and professionally. The group engages with patients daily through the delivery of its pharmacy services, including the expanded range of clinical consultations under Pharmacy First and related advanced services.
The group works closely with NHS commissioners, integrated care systems, and local health partners on the shaping and delivery of service offerings. The Directors use these processes to understand the views and needs of patients and commissioners, to consider the impact of their decisions on patient access and outcomes, and to respond effectively to evolving healthcare needs.
Suppliers
The Directors aim to ensure that the group operates fairly, transparently, and with integrity in its dealings with suppliers. The group engages with and monitors key suppliers around ethical, environmental, and sustainability matters, with regular feedback and dialogue. The Directors seek to maintain strong relationships with key suppliers to ensure best value, support medicine availability for patients, and maintain quality service delivery.
The group's relationships with suppliers have been particularly important during 2024/25 in navigating medicine supply challenges and managing the increased time required to source medicines for patients. The Directors engage with suppliers daily through both formal and informal channels, enabling the business to better understand supply chain dynamics and shape its procurement strategy accordingly.
NHS and Commissioners
The group works constructively with NHS England, integrated care systems, and local commissioners to deliver contracted services and support wider health priorities. The directors engage actively with sector representatives to contribute to policy development and advocate for sustainable funding arrangements.
During 2024/25, the group has supported the successful implementation of Pharmacy First, expanded clinical services, and collaborated with NHS partners to shift care closer to patients' homes in line with government policy. The directors have engaged constructively on sector sustainability issues, including through the independent economic analysis process.
Communities
The group is committed to serving the healthcare needs of local communities, recognising that community pharmacies are often the most accessible healthcare provider for patients. The group's branches play a vital role in their communities, particularly for working adults, families with children, and those facing barriers to accessing GP appointments.
Environmental Responsibility
Environmental matters are taken into consideration by the directors as part of their decision-making process, to minimise the company's impact on the environment wherever possible. The group seeks to implement sustainable practices across its operations, recognising its responsibility to operate in an environmentally conscious manner.

STRATEGIC REPORT (CONTINUED)
FOR THE YEAR ENDED 31 MARCH 2025
- 7 -
Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) Considerations
The group is committed to reducing its environmental impact, supporting local communities, and upholding high standards of governance. Initiatives during 2024/25 have included:
Reducing waste and improving energy efficiency across pharmacy sites, recognising the impact of energy costs on operational sustainability
Supporting local health campaigns and public health initiatives, including expanded blood pressure checks and contraception services
Delivering Pharmacy First services to improve access to treatment for common conditions and reduce pressure on GP services and urgent care
Promoting diversity, equity, and inclusion within the workforce
Ensuring robust governance, compliance with regulatory standards, and adherence to clinical safety protocols
Training staff in information governance and safe management of patient data as digital integration with NHS systems expands
Equal Opportunities and Diversity
The company maintains a policy of equal opportunities in all aspects of employment. The company's employees are vital to its success, and the directors understand that it is critical to engage with and understand their views and to ensure that all employees' interests are considered. Throughout the company there is consultation at all levels of staff on matters of concern. The consultations evolve to meet the changing needs of the company and are valued by all stakeholders.
Diversity and inclusion are key aspects of the company's strong value system and culture, which are articulated in the Diversity Policy. The company never makes any employment-related decisions based upon a person's race, colour, gender, age, religion, disability, sexual orientation, or any other basis protected by law.
The group recognises the business and social benefits of employing people with disabilities and offers support and assistance wherever practically possible. Equality and diversity are embedded in the employment policies of the group, and we aim to ensure fairness through our recruitment and retention processes.
The Directors, either directly or indirectly, ensure that all employees are actively engaged to facilitate their integration into the business and to ensure that opportunities for contribution and development are maximised.
Stakeholder Relationships
The company's patients, customers, commissioners, and suppliers are fundamental to the success of the company. The company strives to continually improve and strengthen its service delivery and stakeholder relationships for the mutual benefit of all parties.
The company has adopted a policy of dealing with creditworthy clients and maintains appropriate credit control procedures. The directors understand the need for effective debtor management and liaise with clients to minimise any risk of non-payment.
The directors' intentions are to behave responsibly toward all stakeholders and to treat them fairly and equally to ensure everyone benefits from the long-term success of the company.
Corporate Governance
The directors have overall responsibility for determining the company's purpose, values, and strategy, and for ensuring high standards of governance. The primary aim of the directors is to promote sustainable success for the long-term benefit of the company, generating value for all stakeholders.
Throughout the next financial year, the directors will continue to review and challenge how the company can improve its engagement with all stakeholders, while navigating the continued challenges facing the community pharmacy sector. The directors remain committed to operating with integrity, transparency, and in the best interests of the company, its stakeholders, and the patients and communities we serve.

At each reporting period end date, the group reviews the carrying amounts of its tangible and intangible assets to determine whether there is any indication that those assets have suffered an impairment loss. If any such indication exists, the recoverable amount of the asset is estimated in order to determine the extent of the impairment loss (if any). Where it is not possible to estimate the recoverable amount of an individual asset, the company estimates the recoverable amount of the cash-generating unit to which the asset belongs.
The carrying amount of the investments accounted for using the equity method is tested for impairment as a single asset. Any goodwill included in the carrying amount of the investment is not tested separately for impairment.
Recoverable amount is the higher of fair value less costs to sell and value in use. In assessing value in use, the estimated future cash flows are discounted to their present value using a pre-tax discount rate that reflects current market assessments of the time value of money and the risks specific to the asset for which the estimates of future cash flows have not been adjusted.
If the recoverable amount of an asset (or cash-generating unit) is estimated to be less than its carrying amount, the carrying amount of the asset (or cash-generating unit) is reduced to its recoverable amount. An impairment loss is recognised immediately in profit or loss, unless the relevant asset is carried at a revalued amount, in which case the impairment loss is treated as a revaluation decrease.
